concerns.text: The primary evaluation (MAE, R², TOST, Hotelling’s T²) is performed on a held‑out test set that is derived from the same DFT‑computed IR spectra and DFT‑computed target properties used for training. Because both predictor (IR spectrum) and outcome (dipole, polarizability, HOMO‑LUMO gap) originate from the same underlying quantum‑chemical calculation, the validation target is not independent of the predictor. This makes the main validation circular: the model is essentially learning to reproduce the DFT method it was fed, rather than demonstrating that vibrational spectra contain independent information about electronic properties. Independent validation on experimental spectra or on data generated with a different DFT functional is marked as optional, leaving the core claim unsupported by truly independent evidence.
